symptom: An L3-21 same-task Director quality-repair edit reduced tests/test_product.py from about 15 KB with 34 discovered tests to a 2176-byte import-only file. Python syntax validation passed, unittest then reported Ran 0 tests, and the repair convergence classifier mislabeled the smaller diagnostic set as progress.

dynamic_evidence.task_contract: TASK-3 test owner; PM and Chief Engineer were not restarted
dynamic_evidence.first_edit_effect: One local test method received a comment; file structure remained intact.
dynamic_evidence.destructive_edit_arguments: search contained the complete existing test file; replace contained only module docstring and imports.
dynamic_evidence.precommit_observation: The edit_file candidate passed Python syntax validation and was physically committed with an authoritative effect receipt.
dynamic_evidence.postcommit_observation: unittest discovery changed from Ran 34 tests with ordinary failures to Ran 0 tests; delivery-depth evidence also collapsed.
dynamic_evidence.owner_drift_observation: The deterministic pass claimed TASK-3 and recorded tests/test_product.py as its in-scope diagnostic target, but the LLM fallback discarded that evidence, preferred a later non-test path from the same mixed verifier blob, and rotated subsequent repair attempts across TASK-2 and TASK-1.
dynamic_evidence.pathless_test_depth_observation: After the missing main function was physically repaired, the exact final provider request still leased TASK-2 production files for Ran 0 tests plus test_source_files/test_assertion_count shortfalls. The Director response correctly stated the defect was test-side and impossible within its exposed production edit paths.

root_causes: write_file enforced a destructive-shrink precommit guard, but edit_file did not enforce the same invariant, allowing full-file search/short-fragment replacement to bypass the write safety policy.

workspace_quality_verifier_regressed parsed unittest failure/error totals but not the authoritative Ran N tests count; Ran 0 tests without a FAILED(...) footer returned no count and escaped regression classification.
A syntax-success receipt proves only parseability, not preservation of test discovery or verifier evidence; diagnostic cardinality alone was therefore unsafe as repair progress authority.

The LLM fallback reran broad diagnostic path heuristics after TaskRuntime had already claimed an exact in-scope owner target. Mixed test/import diagnostics therefore moved the repair away from the current task owner and caused unrelated destructive edits.

The production-depth fallback matched the generic delivery_depth_contract_failed envelope instead of a concrete production metric. A pure test-file/assertion shortfall therefore enumerated src files and leased TASK-2. Pathless test diagnostics also failed to recover the exact same-run CE/JobToken test targets, including the delegated tests/test_behavior.py artifact.
fixes: Apply the existing generic destructive-shrink threshold to edit_file candidates before physical mutation; rejected candidates retain identical workspace bytes and return retryable destructive_shrink evidence.
Parse unittest Ran N tests evidence and classify any post-repair discovered-test count reduction as verifier regression before diagnostic-cardinality progress heuristics.

Carry the deterministic round's TaskRuntime owner evidence into the same-round LLM fallback. Treat it as authoritative only when all supplied owner targets are present in the current diagnostic set; broader stale owner scope remains non-authoritative.

Require a concrete production-depth metric before enumerating production source targets. For pathless test discovery/depth residuals, rehydrate same-run CE blueprint and JobToken authority and route only the declared test artifacts to their Director owner.
Keep recovery scoped to the same Director task and failed verifier; no PM/Chief Engineer restart or target-project manual patch is permitted.

verification.red_tests: Both new regressions failed before implementation: destructive edit_file returned ok=true and Ran 34 to Ran 0 classified as progress.
verification.green_tests: 75/75 tests passed across Director execution tools, Factory workspace-quality characterization, and Python path/diagnostic routing, including current-owner preservation, stale-owner rejection, pure test-depth non-production routing, and frozen CE test-owner recovery; ruff passed; mypy passed for all changed source files.
verification.live_revalidation: Pending isolated-instance restart and same-run quality-gate retry on current Polaris source.

residual_risk: Non-syntactic semantic regressions that preserve file size and test count still depend on affected verifier revalidation. They remain rejected as regression evidence and must be repaired by the same Director task; they must never restart PM or Chief Engineer.
